conclusion.root_cause: In CashInService.cashIn, the burst block calls GameAssets.burst for every collected cube. Milestones get GameAssets.burst(pos, tierColor, 30), and the else branch calls GameAssets.burst(pos) for ordinary cubes. The spec says only milestone counts (1/10/50/100) should fire a GameAssets.burst sparkle. A patched GameAssets.burst saw 101 calls for 101 cash-ins, all with a single argument, so burst fired on every cube including ordinary ones. None of those calls carried the milestone arguments (color, 30), so the milestone case was never distinguished. The checker, which counts milestone-only bursts, therefore found 0 matching calls. I did not establish why `milestone` never evaluated true in my probe; I suspect sentTotal had already advanced past the milestone counts, but I did not check.
conclusion.evidence: Probe 7 patched GameAssets.burst and ran 101 CashInService.cashIn calls at one position. It recorded calls=101, every call with args=1. So burst fires for ordinary cubes, and no call carried the 3-argument milestone form (pos, tierColor, 30). The source from probes 5 and 6 shows the unconditional `else GameAssets.burst(burstInfo.part.Position) end` branch for non-milestone cubes.
conclusion.fix_hint: Call GameAssets.burst only when `milestone` is true, e.g. `if milestone then GameAssets.burst(burstInfo.part.Position, tierColor, 30); burstDone = true end`. For ordinary cubes, drop the GameAssets.burst call and use only the collector's own emitter (`burstInfo.emitter:Emit(8)`). Also confirm sentTotal[player] counts from 1 per player so totals 1, 10, 50 and 100 are hit.

local GREEN = Color3.fromRGB(70, 255, 120)
local RED = Color3.fromRGB(255, 60, 60)
local DENY_DEBOUNCE = 1
local CHECK_INTERVAL = 0.5

type Entry = {
	owner: Player,
	cost: number,
	highlight: Highlight?,
	tween: Tween?,
	active: boolean,
	ancestryConn: RBXScriptConnection?,
	tagOrig: { [TextLabel]: Color3 },
	flashing: boolean,
}

local PadFeedback = {}

local entries: { [BasePart]: Entry } = {}
local cashConns: { [Player]: RBXScriptConnection } = {}
local deniedAt: { [Player]: { [BasePart]: number } } = {}
local remote: RemoteEvent
local affordableEvent: BindableEvent

local function getCash(player: Player): number?
	local ls = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	if not ls then
		return nil
	end
	local cash = ls:FindFirstChild("Cash")
	if cash and (cash:IsA("IntValue") or cash:IsA("NumberValue")) then
		return cash.Value
	end
	return nil
end

local function tagLabels(pad: BasePart): { TextLabel }
	local out = {}
	local roots: { Instance } = { pad }
	if pad.Parent and pad.Parent:IsA("Model") then
		table.insert(roots, pad.Parent)
	end
	for _, root in roots do
		for _, d in root:GetDescendants() do
			if d:IsA("TextLabel") and d:FindFirstAncestorWhichIsA("BillboardGui") then
				table.insert(out, d)
			end
		end
		if #out > 0 then
			break
		end
	end
	return out
end

local function deactivate(pad: BasePart, e: Entry)
	if e.tween then
		e.tween:Cancel()
		e.tween = nil
	end
	if e.highlight then
		e.highlight:Destroy()
		e.highlight = nil
	end
	for label, col in e.tagOrig do
		if label.Parent then
			label.TextColor3 = col
		end
	end
	e.tagOrig = {}
	e.active = false
	if pad.Parent then
		pad:SetAttribute("Affordable", false)
	end
end

local function activate(pad: BasePart, e: Entry)
	e.active = true
	pad:SetAttribute("Affordable", true)
	local h = Instance.new("Highlight")
	h.Name = "AffordHighlight"
	h.FillColor = GREEN
	h.FillTransparency = 0.6
	h.OutlineColor = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	h.OutlineTransparency = 0
	h.DepthMode = Enum.HighlightDepthMode.AlwaysOnTop
	h.Adornee = pad
	h.Enabled = true
	h.Parent = pad
	e.highlight = h
	local tw = TweenService:Create(h, TweenInfo.new(0.6, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut, -1, true), {
		FillTransparency = 0.85,
	})
	tw:Play()
	e.tween = tw
	for _, label in tagLabels(pad) do
		e.tagOrig[label] = label.TextColor3
		label.TextColor3 = GREEN
	end
	Telemetry.count("highlights", 1)
	-- hook for tests / auto-buy paths: server-only, never changes cash itself
	if affordableEvent then
		affordableEvent:Fire(pad, e.owner, e.cost)
	end
end

local function refresh(pad: BasePart)
	local e = entries[pad]
	if not e then
		return
	end
	local cash = getCash(e.owner)
	local affordable = cash ~= nil and cash >= e.cost
	if affordable and not e.active then
		activate(pad, e)
	elseif not affordable and e.active then
		deactivate(pad, e)
	end
end

local function watchCash(player: Player)
	if cashConns[player] then
		return
	end
	local ls = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	local cash = ls and ls:FindFirstChild("Cash")
	if cash and cash:IsA("ValueBase") then
		cashConns[player] = (cash :: any).Changed:Connect(function()
			for pad, e in entries do
				if e.owner == player then

				end
			end
		end)
	end
end

function PadFeedback.GetAffordablePads(player: Player): { BasePart }
	local out: { BasePart } = {}
	for pad, e in entries do
		if e.owner == player and e.active and pad.Parent then
			table.insert(out, pad)
		end
	end
	return out
end

function PadFeedback.Unregister(pad: BasePart)
	local e = entries[pad]
	if not e then
		return
	end
	entries[pad] = nil
	if e.ancestryConn then
		e.ancestryConn:Disconnect()
	end
	deactivate(pad, e)
end

function PadFeedback.Register(pad: BasePart, owner: Player, cost: number)
	if typeof(pad) ~= "Instance" or not pad:IsA("BasePart") then
		return
	end
	if typeof(owner) ~= "Instance" or not owner:IsA("Player") or type(cost) ~= "number" then
		return
	end
	local e = entries[pad]
	if e then
		e.owner = owner
		e.cost = cost
	else
		local newEntry: Entry = {
			owner = owner,
			cost = cost,
			highlight = nil,
			tween = nil,
			active = false,
			ancestryConn = nil,
			tagOrig = {},
			flashing = false,
		}
		newEntry.ancestryConn = pad.AncestryChanged:Connect(function(_, parent)
			if parent == nil then
				PadFeedback.Unregister(pad)
			end
		end)
		entries[pad] = newEntry
		pad:SetAttribute("Affordable", false)
	end
	watchCash(owner)
	refresh(pad)
end

function PadFeedback.Denied(player: Player, pad: BasePart, cost: number)
	if typeof(player) ~= "Instance" or not player:IsA("Player") then
		return
	end
	if typeof(pad) ~= "Instance" or not pad:IsA("BasePart") then
		return
	end
	local c = if type(cost) == "number" then cost else 0
	local perPlayer = deniedAt[player]
	if not perPlayer then
		perPlayer = {}
		deniedAt[player] = perPlayer
	end
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = perPlayer[pad]
	if last and now - last < DENY_DEBOUNCE then
		return
	end
	perPlayer[pad] = now
	Telemetry.count("pad_denied", 1)
	remote:FireClient(player, "denied", pad, c)

	-- server-side red flash so feedback exists even without client help
	local e = entries[pad]
	if not (e and e.flashing) then
		if e then
			e.flashing = true
		end
		local original = pad.Color
		pad.Color = RED
		task.delay(0.35, function()
			if pad.Parent then
				pad.Color = original
			end
			if e then
				e.flashing = false
			end
		end)
	end
end

local function onPlayerRemoving(player: Player)
	for pad, e in entries do
		if e.owner == player then
			PadFeedback.Unregister(pad)
		end
	end
	local conn = cashConns[player]
	if conn then
		conn:Disconnect()
		cashConns[player] = nil
	end
	deniedAt[player] = nil
end

local function init()
	local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("PadFeedback")
	if existing and existing:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
		remote = existing
	else
		remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
		remote.Name = "PadFeedback"
		remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	end
	local existingBind = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild("PadAffordable")
	if existingBind and existingBind:IsA("BindableEvent") then
		affordableEvent = existingBind
	else
		affordableEvent = Instance.new("BindableEvent")
		affordableEvent.Name = "PadAffordable"
		affordableEvent.Parent = ServerStorage
	end
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(onPlayerRemoving)
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(CHECK_INTERVAL)
			for pad, e in entries do
				watchCash(e.owner)
				refresh(pad)
			end
		end
	end)
end

init()

return PadFeedback

conclusion.root_cause: The Buy press on Card_mult1 was swallowed by client-side gating in ShopUi, not by the server. Card_mult1 requires tier_silver (Silver Ore). ShopUi.refresh/tryBuy only treats a requirement as met if the id is in the client's ownedSet, which is filled by ShopSync. While tier_silver is missing from ownedSet, the card reads 'Locked (needs Silver Ore)', Active=false, and tryBuy returns before BuyUpgrade is fired, so the server never sees the request and Cash and shop_purchases stay unchanged. Cash was not the blocker: 385 against a $300 cost. Once tier_silver was owned and synced, the same card flipped to 'Buy'. A direct BuyUpgrade('mult1') then succeeded on the server (cash 613 to 331, card Owned). The testers' presses therefore hit the card while it was still locked, or while the client had not yet received tier_silver ownership. The Card_mult1 button also sits at the bottom edge of the scroll area (button Y 609 to 669, list bottom 617), so it is mostly clipped. That makes it hard to press in the test, and it is partly a testing artefact. Caveat: the exact timing of ownedSet updates relative to the presses was not directly observed.
conclusion.evidence: Probe 4: Card_mult1 = 'Locked (needs Silver Ore)', Active=false, while tier_silver showed 'Buy' and cash was 385. Probe 5: after buying tier_silver, mult1 became 'Buy' and Active=true. Probe 6: BuyUpgrade('mult1') sent directly was accepted, cash went 613 to 331, card Owned, so the server logic is fine. Probe 7: Card_mult1's button Y 609.6 to 669 against a scroll bottom of 617.6, so it is mostly clipped.
conclusion.fix_hint: Keep ownedSet in sync with the server: have the server send ShopSync after every successful purchase (pad touch and card), and have the client call refresh on each ShopSync and on cash changes. Make tryBuy and refresh rely on that synced set, or drop the client-side requires gate and let the server validate. Optionally make the list scroll to or fully show the card that was just unlocked.

-- check: The CashIn and PurchaseFx remotes must be reachable by the client's primary lookup (ReplicatedStorage.Remotes), so the client connects its cash-in sound/FX handler without a 10s stall
-- covers: anomaly: [ServerScriptService/CashInService.luau] Sounds are effectively silent. The census shows sounds_played=0 and client_sounds_played=0
-- consumer: StarterPlayerScripts/CashInFx.client.luau:208
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local StarterPlayer = game:GetService("StarterPlayer")

local cfgModule = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("CashInConfig")
if not cfgModule then error("setup: no CashInConfig") end
local Config = require(cfgModule)
local cashName = Config.CASHIN_REMOTE
local purchName = Config.PURCHASE_REMOTE
if type(cashName) ~= "string" or type(purchName) ~= "string" then
	error("setup: remote names missing in CashInConfig")
end

-- Wait (bounded) for the server to have created the remotes somewhere.
local created = forge.waitFor(function()
	return (ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(cashName, true)) and (ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(purchName, true))
end, 8)
if not created then error("setup: CashIn remotes not created by the server") end

local folder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("Remotes")
local function inFolder(name)
	local r = folder and folder:FindFirstChild(name)
	return r ~= nil and r:IsA("RemoteEvent")
end
local cashInFolder = inFolder(cashName)
local purchInFolder = inFolder(purchName)

if cashInFolder and purchInFolder then
	return { ok = true, detail = "both remotes are in ReplicatedStorage.Remotes" }
end

-- Alternative fix: client no longer blocks on the Remotes folder. Inspect the client source if readable.
local clientFixed = false
local srcInfo = "client source unreadable"
local scriptsFolder = StarterPlayer:FindFirstChild("StarterPlayerScripts")
local cs = scriptsFolder and scriptsFolder:FindFirstChild("CashInFx")
if cs then
	local okSrc, src = pcall(function() return (cs :: any).Source end)
	if okSrc and type(src) == "string" and #src > 0 then
		if src:find("folder:WaitForChild%(name, 10%)") then
			srcInfo = "client still does folder:WaitForChild(name, 10)"
		else
			clientFixed = true
			srcInfo = "client no longer blocks 10s on the Remotes folder"
		end
	end
end

return {
	ok = clientFixed,
	detail = string.format(
		"CashIn in Remotes folder: %s, PurchaseFx in Remotes folder: %s (client looks there first and waits 10s each); %s",
		tostring(cashInFolder), tostring(purchInFolder), srcInfo
	),
}

conclusion.root_cause: highlightDropperPad in Game.server.luau highlights the wrong part, so the real buy pad is never enlarged, glowed or made easy to find. It searches only the plot model's descendants for a BasePart whose name contains 'dropper2'. The only match is the physical dropper machine Workspace.Plots.Plot1.Dropper2, which is a machine and not a buy pad. That part was resized to 8x3x8 and turned Neon, and it does nothing when touched. The real buy pad, UpgradePad_dropper2, is created by UpgradeService under a separate folder, Workspace.UpgradePads_<player>, outside the plot root. It stays at the default 4x0.6x4. It sits at (-19, 2, 140), roughly 20 studs from where the player stands at (-25.8, 4, 120). A player who does not see it just wanders, and the tutorial ('Step on the glowing green pad!') stays stuck on step 3. The pad's visibility and CanTouch are also controlled by UpgradeService.refresh, which is not affected by the highlight code. This is a game bug in the targeting, not a testing artefact.
conclusion.evidence: Probe 2: Workspace.Plots.Plot1.Dropper2 has size 8,3,8 (resized by highlightDropperPad), and it is a dropper machine, not a pad.
